rules.heading: HANDOFF — rules and gates, from the session of 2026-09-28
rules.quote: **Read this first in any new session.** It carries an approved plan whose build was cut short when the session ended
rules.says: A new session reads HANDOFF.md first, updates its status lines in place as work lands, and deletes the file only when every gate reads BUILT, gate 10 has run, and nothing under 'Other work still owed' is left.

rules.heading: FIRST STEP OF EVERY NEW SESSION — the owner only presses approve
rules.quote: The gates below exist and are tested, but they switch on only when installed into the session's own settings, and a container is rebuilt every session.
rules.says: Standing fact: the gates are live only when installed into the session's own settings, the container is rebuilt every session, a session cannot install them unasked (Claude Code refuses it as self-modification), and the setup script that would do it is not reachable from the tablet app, so the install must happen inside the first approved plan.

rules.heading: FIRST STEP OF EVERY NEW SESSION — the owner only presses approve
rules.quote: 1. The session's FIRST plan contains exactly this step: clone main, then install FROM THE CLONE, then the probe below.
rules.says: The session's first plan contains exactly the step of cloning main to /root/.claude/hub, running node /root/.claude/hub/hook-dispatch.mjs --install from that clone, then the probe; the plan is approved with the plan button and nothing else is asked of the owner.

rules.heading: FIRST STEP OF EVERY NEW SESSION — the owner only presses approve
rules.quote: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/njefferson/noahjefferson /root/.claude/hub
rules.says: The install step in the first plan uses a shallow clone (depth 1) of the main repository at https://github.com/njefferson/noahjefferson into /root/.claude/hub, then runs node /root/.claude/hub/hook-dispatch.mjs --install.
rules.missing: The shallow clone (--depth 1) and its being the step of the session's first plan; the live script clones without depth and runs from an environment setup script, not a first-plan step.

rules.heading: FIRST STEP OF EVERY NEW SESSION — the owner only presses approve
rules.quote: Never install from the working copy: `install()` wires whichever copy runs it, and a broken edit in a working copy would then refuse its own fix.
rules.says: Never run the hook install from the working copy, only from the stable clone at /root/.claude/hub, because install wires whichever copy runs it and a broken edit would refuse its own fix.

rules.heading: FIRST STEP OF EVERY NEW SESSION — the owner only presses approve
rules.quote: **Measured 2026-09-28, second session:** the install was allowed inside the approved plan, and the gates went live mid-session with no restart.
rules.says: Standing fact: the install is allowed inside an approved plan and the gates go live mid-session with no restart, after which the first ordinary call and the probe are refused.

rules.heading: FIRST STEP OF EVERY NEW SESSION — the owner only presses approve
rules.quote: 2. **Probe, harmless whether the gates are live or not:** write a file in the session scratchpad.
rules.says: Probe the gates by writing a file in the session scratchpad, where a refusal until the next plan is approved (approved-plan-guard) is the proof they are live.

rules.heading: FIRST STEP OF EVERY NEW SESSION — the owner only presses approve
rules.quote: Never probe with a Drive search: if the gates were dead, it would search the owner's Drive.
rules.says: Never probe the gates with a Drive search, because if the gates were dead it would really search the owner's Drive.

rules.heading: FIRST STEP OF EVERY NEW SESSION — the owner only presses approve
rules.quote: 3. If the install is refused even after approval, say so to the owner in one line, record the result here and in LESSONS §370, and carry on
rules.says: If the install is refused even after approval, tell the owner in one line, record the result in HANDOFF.md and LESSONS §370, and carry on, never sending the owner to a settings page.

rules.heading: FIRST STEP OF EVERY NEW SESSION — the owner only presses approve
rules.quote: 4. **Before the install, every repo's working tree must carry a working `plan-guard.sh`** (measured 2026-09-29).
rules.says: Before installing, every repo's working tree must carry a working plan-guard.sh, because the dispatcher runs each repo's own hooks from its working tree and an old shim refuses every plan-mode call including ExitPlanMode; JPS main has the old shim, so check JPS out on a branch carrying the fix (claude/laughing-edison-x0pdv8) first.

rules.heading: FIRST STEP OF EVERY NEW SESSION — the owner only presses approve
rules.quote: **Then plan twice.** A plan approved before the install minted no marker, so the first write after it is refused (the probe), and the work goes up again as the next plan.
rules.says: After installing, plan twice: the plan approved before the install minted no marker so the first write is refused and the work is submitted again as the next plan, and because the ledger starts empty the first command after that approval re-reads every SHA the plan cites.

rules.heading: The root cause, measured
rules.quote: **None of the owner's hooks ran for the whole session.** The session was launched in `/home/user`, the parent of both repos
rules.says: Standing fact: Claude Code loads project hooks only from the launch directory, so a session launched in the parent /home/user (no .claude/settings.json) runs none of the owner's hooks, only the cloud environment's own stop-hook-git-check.sh, meaning every gate is dead unless installed at user level.
rules.live_quote: Two repositories in the session: the dispatcher prints one line at the start and at each resume, naming them. None of them loaded its own roles, settings or instruction file.
rules.missing: The general fact that project hooks load only from the launch directory, that a session launched in a parent folder runs none of the owner's hooks (only the cloud environment's stop-hook-git-check.sh), and that gates are dead unless installed at user level.

rules.heading: The root cause, measured
rules.quote: The hub's CLAUDE.md already recorded this exact failure for `branch-guard` ("a session rooted in a PARENT directory never fires").
rules.says: Standing fact: a session rooted in a parent directory never fires any project hook, as the hub's CLAUDE.md already recorded for branch-guard.
rules.live_quote: If the hub's repository sits beside it, say so and stop: started that way, the app's own roles and settings do not load.
rules.missing: The statement that a session rooted in a parent directory never fires any project hook (and branch-guard as the recorded case); only the two-repositories-side-by-side case is stated.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: 1. **Tell the owner in the first line, all during the work, and at the end.** The first line says what is being done now and what comes next.
rules.says: The first line of a reply says what is being done now and what comes next.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: During the work, each step says what it is, what it found in plain terms, and what that means.
rules.says: During the work, each step states what it is, what it found in plain terms, and what that means.
rules.live_quote: Report what changed and what it means, in plain words, with the state at the end: finished, paused on what, or running what.
rules.missing: That it applies during the work to each step (what the step is and what it found), not only to the report of a finished piece; the live line is about the final report.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: Anything long says how long it takes and the clock time of the next report.
rules.says: Anything long states how long it will take and the clock time of the next report.
rules.live_quote: **Say what it will cost BEFORE a long run**, in seconds or minutes, and let it be stopped.
rules.missing: The clock time of the next report; only the duration/cost before a long run is stated.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: At the end: what was done, what was not, what was found and not fixed, and what is open for the owner.
rules.says: At the end of the work, report what was done, what was not, what was found and not fixed, and what is open for the owner.
rules.live_quote: Report what changed and what it means, in plain words, with the state at the end: finished, paused on what, or running what.
rules.missing: The required end-report contents: what was not done, and what is open for the owner (only the worker role's 'Found' lines cover found-and-not-fixed).

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: Process noise with no finding in it is not telling.
rules.says: Process noise with no finding in it does not count as telling the owner.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: 2. **A status at least every five minutes during any work**, saying what is done, what is running, what is next and when the next status comes.
rules.says: During any work give a status at least every five minutes saying what is done, what is running, what is next and when the next status comes; hours with no idea when the next report arrives, or a bare 'Working...', is the silence the owner means.
rules.live_quote: A silent five minutes is the shape of the failure this section
rules.missing: Only a passing mention that a silent five minutes is a failure, inside the cost-before-a-long-run rule. Missing: a status at least every five minutes, naming what is done, running, next and when the next status comes; a bare 'Working...' counting as silence.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: 3. **No app notifications, ever.** Statuses go in chat and on the status page.
rules.says: Never send app notifications; statuses go in chat and on the status page.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: 4. **Reply to every point in a message from the owner.** Skipping part of it is ignoring it.
rules.says: Reply to every point in an owner's message, since skipping part of it is ignoring it.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: A message saying something was done wrong is a full stop: answer it, and nothing else runs in that turn.
rules.says: When a message from the owner says something was done wrong, answer it and run nothing else in that turn.
rules.live_quote: A question from the owner gets an answer and nothing else.
rules.missing: The case of a message saying something was done wrong (a complaint is a full stop: answer it and run nothing else); only questions are covered.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: 5. **Plan mode only.** Nothing runs outside a plan the owner approved.
rules.says: Work in plan mode only: nothing runs outside a plan the owner approved.
rules.live_quote: Plan mode for the scope, because it gives the approve button.
rules.missing: That plan mode is the only mode and that nothing runs outside a plan the owner approved; the live page uses plan mode for the scope and a non-asking mode for the run.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: Before a plan goes up, one chat turn says what is being done and why, and asks nothing. It never pastes the plan's text
rules.says: Before a plan goes up, one chat turn says what is being done and why, asks nothing, and never pastes the plan's text, since the owner reads the plan in the plan.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: After the owner's reply, the next turn ends with ExitPlanMode.
rules.says: After the owner replies to the pre-plan chat turn, the next turn ends with ExitPlanMode.
rules.live_quote: **AND A PLAN-MODE TURN ENDS WITH THE TOOL, NEVER WITH PROSE.** ... The approve control only appears when `ExitPlanMode` is called
rules.missing: That the ExitPlanMode turn comes after the owner's reply to the pre-plan chat turn (the talk-first sequence).

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: Approval is only the plan-mode button.
rules.says: Approval counts only when given by the plan-mode button, and a reply asking for approval in chat is refused.
rules.live_quote: Approval is only the button. A typed word approves nothing.
rules.missing: That a reply asking for approval in chat is refused (stop-guard); the live line covers only that the button alone approves.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: 6. **A line before each tool call and a line after each result.**
rules.says: Write a line before each tool call and a line after each result.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: 7. **Never "waiting on you", never "you owe".** Say "open for you:".
rules.says: Never write 'waiting on you' or 'you owe'; say 'open for you:' instead.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: 8. **A limit is reported only after every route available was tried**, with the failed attempt named.
rules.says: Report a limit to the owner only after every available route has been tried, naming the failed attempt (for example try the Drive connector's own download before saying a private Drive folder cannot be read).
rules.live_quote: hands the owner the work. It is nearly always wrong, and the reason it is wrong is always the same — **the wrong thing was tried first, and nothing else was tried at all.**
rules.missing: The general rule for any limit (not only network access): report it only after every available route was tried, naming the failed attempt, e.g. the Drive connector's download before saying a private Drive folder cannot be read.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: 9. **A defect of the session is a bug**, never framed as the owner's preference or "your rule".
rules.says: Treat a defect of the session as a bug and never frame it as the owner's preference or 'your rule'.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: 10. **When the harness reports ultracode off, the first line of the next reply says so.**
rules.says: When the harness reports ultracode off, the first line of the next reply says so.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: The session silently dropped work when it went off.
rules.says: When ultracode goes off, a session must not silently drop work; the loss is to be named in the first line of the next reply.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: **And on 2026-09-28 the harness twice reported ultracode off while it was on.** That notice is a harness bug.
rules.says: The ultracode-off notice is a known harness bug (it twice reported off while on), so when it appears the first line says so and the work continues with ultracode on.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: 11. **Questions to the owner are real decisions only** — never something the record already ranks, never research handed back.
rules.says: Ask the owner only real decisions, never something the record already ranks and never research handed back.
rules.live_quote: A choice is offered only where each option leaves the work whole and the record cannot rank them.
rules.missing: That research is never handed back to the owner; the live lines cover only that choices are offered when the record cannot rank them.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: 12. **Infrared first.** A white-balance test that moved only the red and blue sliders with green fixed is a visible-light model, and was rejected.
rules.says: Treat infrared first: a white-balance test that moves only the red and blue sliders with green fixed is a visible-light model and is rejected.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: In this app a neutral's colour is set by the black level (one number: the four per-site values in MakerNote 0x3D averaged;
rules.says: Standing fact about the app: a neutral's colour is set by the black level (one number, the four MakerNote 0x3D per-site values averaged, reading 1008 on all seven owner raws traced 2026-09-29), the lens profile's colour, gray-world's three gains, the look's 3x3 mixer (swap and infrared subtraction), its tint, per-channel curves and grade wheels, per IR-SCIENCE.md sections 3, 4c and 6.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: 13. **Search the whole codebase before saying a name is real or invented.**
rules.says: Search the whole codebase before telling the owner a name is real or invented, since a partial search reported as fact is the defect in either direction (for example wbBias in src/main.ts).

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: 14. **Look at everything from the owner's side.** Never hand the owner a step a session can do.
rules.says: Never hand the owner a step a session can do; ask the owner only for what only they can do.
rules.live_quote: - Never send the owner on a goose chase. Don't hand over a manual step unless you have either (a) verified that exact step end-to-end yourself, or (b) proven it is impossible
rules.missing: The live line allows handing over a step the session verified it could do (option a); the old rule never hands the owner a step a session can do, and asks only what only the owner can do.

rules.heading: The rules (2026-09-28) — each one broken in that session
rules.quote: Anything asked of the owner is only what only they can do, doable in the tablet app with a tap or a reply — an approve button, a one-word answer.
rules.says: Whatever is asked of the owner must be doable in the tablet app with a tap or a reply (an approve button, a one-word answer), never directions to settings, a menu, a setup script, a permission rule or an install, and every route must be tried first.
rules.live_quote: When work stops on something only the owner can do, say so as a need: that work is stopped, what is needed and where it is done, why, what it holds up, and what is not known.
rules.missing: That what is asked of the owner must be doable in the tablet app with a tap or a reply, and never directions to settings, a menu, a setup script, a permission rule or an install.

rules.heading: The gates — the approved plan, with build status
rules.quote: Each gate is made to fail once on a planted payload before it is trusted.
rules.says: Each gate must be made to fail once on a planted payload before it is trusted.
rules.live_quote: - Make a new test FAIL once before trusting it.

rules.heading: The gates — the approved plan, with build status
rules.quote: - **1. `hook-dispatch.mjs`** — BUILT (d578392), planted: install, write refusal outside a plan, reads pass, Stop runs once
rules.says: Standing fact: hook-dispatch.mjs, wired once at user level, per event runs the hub's family guards then each touched repo's own .claude/settings.json hooks with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set to that repo (touched repo is the one holding the edited path or the Bash working directory, every repo for pathless tools, skipping the launch-directory repo), first deny wins, a crash in PreToolUse refuses everything but reads, it runs from the stable clone at /root/.claude/hub, and --install writes ~/.claude/settings.json.
rules.live_quote: `hook-dispatch.mjs` is the one dispatcher. It refuses the choice popup, runs `push-guard.mjs`, brings the hub's copy forward at a start, runs each repository's own hooks
rules.missing: Which repositories are touched and how CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is set per repo, skipping the launch-directory repo; first deny wins; wired once at user level; that --install writes ~/.claude/settings.json; running from the stable clone (only the push-guard-failure refusal is in running.md:41).

rules.heading: The gates — the approved plan, with build status
rules.quote: **1. `hook-dispatch.mjs`** — BUILT (d578392), planted: install, write refusal outside a plan, reads pass, Stop runs once, the post-compaction tool list prints.
rules.says: The dispatcher must, after a context compaction, print the post-compaction tool list, must run the Stop hooks only once per Stop, and is wired once at user level so it fires however a session is rooted.
rules.live_quote: The hub's copy is at `/root/.claude/hub` and its dispatcher is wired.
rules.missing: The post-compaction tool list, Stop hooks running once per Stop, and that it is wired once at user level so it fires however a session is rooted; only 'its dispatcher is wired' is stated.

rules.heading: The gates — the approved plan, with build status
rules.quote: **Fixed 6592f28:** - a family guard that crashes refuses every non-read;
rules.says: The dispatcher behaviours fixed in 6592f28 are required: a crashing family guard refuses every non-read, --mark's outcome is passed to the session, only the hub's own report.mjs is exempt from the report clock, and --install keeps the clear-context-on-accept option off because that approval route mints no marker.
rules.live_quote: when the push guard fails to run, the dispatcher refuses every tool that is not a read, and says so in its refusal line, until the guard is fixed.
rules.missing: --mark's outcome passed to the session, only report.mjs exempt from the report clock, and --install keeping the clear-context-on-accept option off; only the crash-refuses-non-reads part is stated (for the push guard).

rules.heading: The gates — the approved plan, with build status
rules.quote: - **1a. report-clock** — BUILT (`report.mjs`, d578392), planted 4 of 4. `report.mjs "<status>"` stamps the time.
rules.says: Run report.mjs "<status>" to stamp the report time; PreToolUse refuses every call (reads too) once five minutes pass since the last stamp, measured from the owner's last message, with report.mjs itself and subagent calls (payload agent_id) exempt.

rules.heading: The gates — the approved plan, with build status
rules.quote: - **2. approved-plan-guard** — BUILT, and its approval half WORKS since 5c3b094.
rules.says: Standing fact: approved-plan-guard recognises a real approval by reading the result's filePath (planted 21 ways) and writes the marker; it formerly never wrote a marker because --mark matched phrases that exist only in the sentence shown to the session.

rules.heading: The gates — the approved plan, with build status
rules.quote: **Fixed 2566674, found by the review of that fix:** - the `--done` exception is granted only on its real condition;
rules.says: approved-plan-guard must grant the --done exception only on its real condition, refuse when its classifier crashes, refuse an unreadable plan file with its reason, void the approval on any edit to the approved plan (saying so in the refusal), count an approval only in the session that gave it, and say in a refusal that the action is not a recognised read and quote why.

rules.heading: The gates — the approved plan, with build status
rules.quote: - **3. plan-guard, talk-first** — BUILT (efb9a93), planted both ways. ExitPlanMode refused unless, since the last rejected ExitPlanMode or the last EnterPlanMode, a turn ended in assistant text and a genuine owner message followed it.
rules.says: ExitPlanMode is refused unless, since the last rejected ExitPlanMode or the last EnterPlanMode, a turn ended in assistant text and a genuine owner message followed it.
